name: shaderous

tools.name: describe
tools.description: List the problems (presets) with their ids, dimensions, end times and parameters, and the fields, variables and choices a setup can make. Give `problem` for one problem in full, with its description.

problem.description: A problem id for its full entry

tools.name: check_setup
tools.description: Check a setup document before running it. Returns `ok`, an `error` if it cannot be read at all (with the key at fault), `notes` (keys dropped, values held to their range), and `issues`: each with a level (`error`: a rule broken, such as a star without isolated self-gravity, or a value that cannot work; `warning`: a choice to look at again, such as a softening under two cells, bodies that overlap or leave the box, a grid past the GPU memory), a sentence, and the path of the part or option it is about. Use it after writing or changing a document and before `load`.

tools.name: load
tools.description: Build a new run from a setup and leave it paused at t = 0. A setup is a preset with overrides, or a whole setup document (`document`) that assembles a run from parts: point masses, stars, disks, gas regions, obstacles, a magnetic field. The setup uses the keys of a shareable link, as a query string ("problem=sedov&dim=2&n=512&gamma=1.4") or an object ({"problem": "sedov", "dim": 2, "n": 512}). Returns the run’s state, including `query`, the setup in force.

setup.description: Query string, link, or object of setup keys; or a setup document itself

document.description: A setup document (format "shaderous-setup", see docs/setups.md and describe().setup): the run is built from it, and `setup` then says the grid and what differs. Start from preset(id) to make one

tools.name: run
tools.description: Advance the run: to time `until` (the last step is shortened to land on it exactly), by `steps` steps, or whichever comes first. Stops at the problem’s end time (stopped: "end"); to go further, load with a later `tend`. Returns t, dt, steps, steps taken, wall seconds and why it stopped.

until.description: Run until the clock reads this time

steps.description: Take at most this many steps

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this much wall time (default 600)

tools.name: state
tools.description: The run: problem, dimensions, grid, amr levels, time, timestep, steps, end time, whether it has finished, the GPU adapter, and `query`, the setup that reproduces it.

tools.name: diagnostics
tools.description: Totals and extremes read back now: mass, momentum, kinetic/internal/gravitational/total energy, max Mach number, floored cells, Jeans-unresolved cells, center of mass, point masses, and the [min, max] of every field.

tools.name: stats
tools.description: Least, greatest and volume-weighted mean of each variable over the box (rho, press, vel1-3, r0 and species mass fractions).

tools.name: slice
tools.description: A variable on a res x res grid on a plane through the box (perpendicular to `axis` at fraction `pos`). Returns min, max and mean, and the values (row j, column i: values[j][i]) when res is at most 64 or include_values is set; with save_path the full slice is written there instead: as a .npy file (float32, shape [res, res], for numpy’s np.load) when the name ends in .npy, else as JSON.

variable.description: One of rho, press, vel1, vel2, vel3, r0, level, temp, tempK, or the name of a species. temp is the temperature in code units, tempK in kelvin (a setup with physical units). Default rho

res.description: Default: the size of the grid, at most 256 (the MCP tool: 32)

include_values.description: Return the values at any res (default: only when res is at most 64)

save_path.description: Write the slice to this file: .npy (float32 for numpy), else JSON

tools.name: probe
tools.description: The gas at points given as fractions of the box ([x, y, z], z ignored in 2D): density, pressure, velocity, passive scalar, temperature (temp in code units; tempK in kelvin, with physical units), refinement level and species mass fractions.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: A picture of the run as a PNG image. `view` changes what is drawn first: mode (volume|slice|projection), field (index, see describe), species, log, lo, hi, sliceAxis, slicePos, minRho, opacity, yaw, pitch, dist, tx, ty, tz, zoom, cx, cy, showBlocks, contours, nContours, fog, surfaceOpacity, light, box, fieldLines, fieldLineCount, colormap, autoRange. Settings persist for later screenshots.

save_path.description: Also write the PNG to this file

tools.name: view
tools.description: Change what screenshots show without touching the run. Returns the view settings.

changes.description: Any of mode, field, species, log, lo, hi, sliceAxis, slicePos, minRho, opacity, yaw, pitch, dist, tx, ty, tz, zoom, cx, cy, showBlocks, contours, nContours, fog, surfaceOpacity, light, box, fieldLines, fieldLineCount, colormap, autoRange

tools.name: controls
tools.description: The control panel as it stands: every control’s id, kind, label, tooltip, value and options. Use with `control` to change settings mid-run.

tools.name: control
tools.description: Set a panel control (or press a button, with no value) exactly as a person would, mid-run, and wait for what it starts (a shader rebuild, a restart). Examples: control("riemann", "hll"), control("eos", "gas_radiation"), control("reset"). Number fields take values in the units the panel shows; set control("units", "code") first for code units. The run stays paused.

tools.name: restart
tools.description: Start the run again from its initial conditions, paused.

tools.name: save_athdf
tools.description: Save the state of the gas to an .athdf file (HDF5 in Athena++’s layout; yt reads it). The file carries the setup, so load_athdf continues the run exactly.

path.description: File or folder to write to (default: the current folder, under the file’s own name)

tools.name: record
tools.description: Record the run from where it is as an MP4 movie (H.264), stepping it as it goes: the current view with a color bar, x/y/z axes and the status line (grid, simulation time) over it. A frame every `every` steps, or near every `dt` of code time (at the nearest step boundary: no step is shortened, so the run is the one it would have been unrecorded). Stops at `until`, after `frames` frames, or at the end time. Set the view first. Returns the frame count, movie length and where the file went.

path.description: File or folder to write to (default: the current folder, under the name of the movie)

dt.description: A frame near every multiple of this much code time (default: a 600th of the dynamical time of the problem, so one dynamical time plays in 10 s at 60 fps)

every.description: Or a frame every this many steps

until.description: Stop when the clock reaches this time (landed on exactly)

height.description: Default 1080 (9/16 of width when width is given)

bitrate_mbps.description: Megabits per second of movie (default 0.2 bits per pixel per frame: 25 at 1080p and 60 fps)

status.description: The status line (grid, simulation time, point masses, mesh). Default true

timeout_s.description: Give up after this much wall time, keeping what was recorded

tools.name: load_athdf
tools.description: Start a run from an .athdf file: one Shaderous wrote continues exactly; another code’s is loaded into the current problem. Paused at the file’s time.

tools.name: debris
tools.description: Debris energies, for problems that track them (describe: problems[].debris, e.g. tidal-disruption): the gas binned by its specific orbital energy about the point mass, both what has left the box (tallied as it left) and what is in it, a surviving self-bound core set apart, and the return rate of the bound debris to pericenter, dM/dt (Kepler). Returns totals, the core, the first return and the peak of dM/dt (in days and solar masses per year where the problem has units). save_path writes the full report (bins, dmdt.t and dmdt.rate) as JSON.

save_path.description: Write the full report as JSON to this file

tools.name: errors
tools.description: What the page has reported going wrong (uncaught errors, failed shader builds, a lost GPU device), oldest first.

instructions:
Shaderous is a GPU gas dynamics code (compressible Euler equations with gravity, cooling, adaptive mesh refinement). These tools drive one simulation in a headless browser.
Typical use: describe (pick a problem) -> load (a setup: problem, dim, n, amr and other keys) -> run (to a time, landed on exactly, or a number of steps) -> diagnostics / stats / slice / probe for numbers, screenshot to look at it -> save_athdf to keep the state, record for a movie.
All values are in code units; positions are fractions of the box (0 to 1). A run stays paused between calls. load restarts from t = 0; control changes a setting mid-run as a person would.
GPU memory (how many blocks the adaptive mesh can hold) is the control "gpumem", in GB: control {id: "gpumem", value: 4} sets it and starts the run again; value "" returns to the guessed default (2.5 GB on a desktop). The server's --gpu-memory option sets it before the first run.
